identification.summary: UNC4841 is Mandiant's designation for a suspected China-nexus espionage actor that exploited the Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG) zero-day CVE-2023-2868 to compromise a subset of ESG appliances worldwide [S1]. Mandiant assessed with high confidence that UNC4841 conducts espionage in support of the People's Republic of China [S1][S2]. Mandiant describes it as well resourced, using a wide range of purpose-built malware and deploying specific families selectively against priority targets, with SKIPJACK the most widely deployed [S2]. About 5% of ESG appliances were compromised [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant: earliest exploit emails observed 2022-10-10 [S1]; first exploitation surge in early November 2022 [S2].
identification.notes: UNC4841 is a Mandiant (Google Cloud) cluster. Mandiant had not attributed it to a previously known group [S2]. No Microsoft name is recorded in this encyclopedia's record for UNC4841. Mandiant notes infrastructure overlap with UNC2286 (GhostEmperor / FamousSparrow), judged likely due to shared anonymization or hosting providers, and a similar REPTILE-derived tooling technique used by UNC3886 (CASTLETAP) [S2]. These are overlaps, not merged clusters. Mandiant's June 2023 report also noted shared infrastructure with other China-nexus operations may reflect a common procurement entity rather than the same group [S1]. CISA tracks DEPTHCHARGE as SUBMARINE [S2].

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China (Mandiant assessment: espionage in support of the PRC) [S1][S2]. No specific PRC organization (MSS, PLA, contractor) is named in the sources gathered.
attribution.confidence: Mandiant: high confidence that UNC4841 is a China-nexus espionage actor supporting the PRC [S1][S2]. Mandiant states that US government agencies independently corroborated this (IC3, August 2023) [S2]. Press reporting says the FBI linked the activity to China [S3]; the underlying FBI document was not opened.
attribution.basis: Targeting aligned with PRC policy priorities, particularly Asia-Pacific and Taiwan, and collection against ASEAN foreign ministries, Taiwan and Hong Kong academics and research organizations [S1]. Infrastructure overlap with UNC2286 [S2]. Mandiant's assessment is the basis; Mandiant did not tie UNC4841 to a previously known group [S2].

objectives: Espionage: bulk and targeted collection of email data from compromised ESG appliances. Scripts searched the ESG email store for specific users or domains, and email data was staged and exfiltrated [S1]. Targeted collection covered ASEAN Ministry of Foreign Affairs staff, foreign trade offices, Taiwan and Hong Kong academics and research organizations, and Southeast Asian government officials [S1]. Mandiant also reports credential harvesting from cleartext credentials in stored messages, followed by Outlook Web Access logins [S2].

sectors: Government (national and local; almost a third of affected organizations) [S1][S2]
High technology and IT, including regional IT and managed service providers [S2]
Healthcare, biotech, aerospace and defense, semiconductors (minority targets) [S2]
regions: Global; victims in at least 16 countries during the May 2023 high-frequency phase [S1]
Americas (most observed activity, which may partly reflect Barracuda's customer base) [S1][S2]
Asia-Pacific, Taiwan, Hong Kong and ASEAN governments (policy-priority targeting) [S1]
targeting.notes: Mandiant observed 26 verticals; local government was about 7% of all victims and about 17% of US-only victims at one point [S2]. Early exploitation hit regional IT and MSP providers, possibly to reach the domains those appliances managed [S2]. Malware such as SKIPJACK, DEPTHCHARGE, FOXTROT and FOXGLOVE was reserved for priority victims; FOXTROT and FOXGLOVE only against high-priority government or government-related targets [S2].

capabilities.summary: Initial access by emailing crafted TAR attachments that exploit CVE-2023-2868, a command injection in ESG attachment scanning where a user-controlled filename reaches a Perl qx{} call [S1]. Early files used .tar; later ones used .jpg or .dat; some emails were sent from already compromised ESG appliances [S1]. Custom tooling included SEASPY (passive PCAP-filter backdoor), SALTWATER (bsmtpd module), SEASIDE (Lua module launching the WHIRLPOOL reverse shell), SANDBAR (kernel rootkit), SEASPRAY and SKIPJACK (trojanized Lua modules) [S1]. After Barracuda's patch, Mandiant observed SEASPY v2 (May 22, 2023), then DEPTHCHARGE, FOXGLOVE and FOXTROT (from May 30, 2023) [S2]. DEPTHCHARGE is loaded into the BSMTP daemon via LD_PRELOAD and its persistence trigger sits in the configuration database, so it can re-infect a clean appliance when an exported configuration is restored [S2]. FOXTROT, derived from open-source REPTILE, and FOXGLOVE were the only families not built for the ESG [S2]. Persistence also used cron jobs, init edits and extra SSH accounts [S1][S2]. Post-exploitation included fscan scanning of more than 50 subnets in one environment, SSH movement to VPNs, proxies and edge devices, timestomping, and exfiltration using openssl s_client and, in limited cases, anonfiles.com [S1][S2]. In December 2023 UNC4841 was reported exploiting a second zero-day, CVE-2023-7102 (Spreadsheet::ParseExcel via the Amavis scanner), deploying new SEASPY and SALTWATER variants to a limited number of devices [S4]. Infrastructure used hosting and VPS providers, default self-signed Barracuda certificates, and ports 8080, then mostly 443 or 25 [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Initial CVE-2023-2868 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Earliest exploit emails with malicious TAR attachments observed on 2022-10-10; first exploitation surge in early November 2022. Early compromises were on appliances geolocated to mainland China using port 8080 for C2 [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Discovery, patch and malware retooling
campaigns.summary: Barracuda discovered the activity 2023-05-19 and began patching 2023-05-20 to 2023-05-21 (sources differ on the exact day). UNC4841 modified its malware within a day, deployed SEASPY v2 on 2023-05-22, and conducted high-frequency operations against victims in at least 16 countries 2023-05-22 to 05-24 [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: Second wave: DEPTHCHARGE, FOXGLOVE, FOXTROT
campaigns.summary: From 2023-05-30 to early June, UNC4841 deployed DEPTHCHARGE, FOXGLOVE and FOXTROT against priority victims, the most intense period of the campaign. Mandiant published its attribution on 2023-06-15. Barracuda advised replacing compromised appliances regardless of patch level [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: FBI warning and Mandiant remediation analysis
campaigns.summary: Press reports the FBI stated Barracuda's patches were ineffective and that all affected ESG appliances should be considered compromised; the FBI document was not opened [S3]. Mandiant's 2023-08-29 follow-up found no new compromises after the patch and described the SKIPJACK, DEPTHCHARGE, FOXTROT and FOXGLOVE tooling [S2].

campaigns.name: CVE-2023-7102 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Barracuda patched CVE-2023-7102 starting 2023-12-21 and pushed a cleanup patch 2023-12-22. Barracuda and Mandiant tied the exploitation to UNC4841, which deployed new SEASPY and SALTWATER variants to a limited number of ESG devices [S4].

diamond.adversary: UNC4841, a China-nexus espionage cluster assessed by Mandiant with high confidence to act for the PRC; not mapped to a known named group [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Zero-day CVE-2023-2868 (and CVE-2023-7102 later), email-borne exploit delivery, bespoke ESG-specific backdoors and rootkit, plus REPTILE-derived FOXTROT for priority targets [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Dozens of IPs on hosting and VPS providers (US, Hong Kong, elsewhere), a small set of domains, ports 8080/443/25, default Barracuda self-signed certificates, and compromised ESG appliances as mail senders [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Government (about a third), technology and IT, telecom, manufacturing, universities, with priority targets in ASEAN, Taiwan and Hong Kong; most activity in the Americas [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection supporting PRC policy priorities, particularly Asia-Pacific and Taiwan [S1].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing email security appliances that sit in the mail path, hold stored mail and credentials, are difficult to monitor with EDR, and trusted with TLS certificates and network position; the vendor advised replacement rather than reimaging [S1][S2].

gaps: No specific PRC sponsor organization (MSS, PLA, contractor) is named in the sources gathered.
No Microsoft name mapping was found for UNC4841; searches for Microsoft or other-vendor equivalents returned nothing, so alias equivalence is unverified.
The existing record lists SLIME57 as an alias with an unspecified vendor; no gathered source states it, so it is not added to aliasesAdd.

Primary documents not opened: FBI/IC3 alert and CISA malware analysis reports (MAR-10454006 series, MAR-10459736), Barracuda advisory, Mandiant hardening guide; cisa.gov is blocked. Press coverage was used for FBI statements.
Conference material referenced in the record (Black Hat Asia 2024, JSAC 2025) was not retrieved; a search did not surface it.
Activity after the December 2023 CVE-2023-7102 exploitation is not documented in the sources gathered; current status of UNC4841 is unknown.
Exact regional and sector percentages in Mandiant's figures were not retrievable in text form.
Overlap with UNC2286 (GhostEmperor / FamousSparrow) and UNC3886 is noted by Mandiant as infrastructure or technique similarity only; the relationship is unresolved [S2].
The December 2023 reporting came through secondary coverage; Barracuda's and Mandiant's original statements were not opened [S4].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Email security gateways and similar edge appliances in the mail path are key cyber terrain; they hold stored mail and credentials and trusted certificates, and are lightly monitored [S1][S2]. STEP 2: Potentially affected battlespace includes government, telecom, IT/MSP and defense-adjacent networks, with ASEAN, Taiwan and Hong Kong policy bodies as priority interest [S1][S2]. STEP 3: The observed pattern is a zero-day against an appliance, retooling within a day of the patch, selective use of heavier implants against priority victims, then credential harvesting from mail and lateral movement via SSH to edge devices [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued mail-path and edge-device exploitation for policy and diplomatic collection. MDCOA is a pre-positioned appliance implant that survives reimaging via configuration-based re-infection (as with DEPTHCHARGE) and is used for collection on US or partner government mail during a Taiwan-related crisis [S1][S2]. Candidate indicators: unexpected cron entries and init modifications on gateways, unfamiliar processes or SSH accounts on appliances, outbound connections from mail appliances on ports 8080/443/25 to hosting-provider IPs, and TAR attachments with unusual extensions [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track vendor end-of-support and emergency advisories for mail and edge appliances, and maintain an inventory of such devices on mission networks, since compromise persisted through patching [S1][S2]. (2) Authorities: replacement of compromised appliances (rather than patching) is a vendor and FBI-level recommendation, so decision authority and funding for hardware replacement should be clarified in advance [S1][S3]. (3) Mission assurance: assume stored mail and credentials on an affected gateway are exposed; plan credential and certificate rotation and alternate communications paths [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3, the DIB cybersecurity program, FBI and coalition partners, given that ASEAN and Taiwan-focused collection implies partner-network exposure [S1][S2].

sources.title: Barracuda ESG Zero-Day Exploited Globally by China-Nexus Actor (CVE-2023-2868)
FBI: Patches for Barracuda ESG Zero-Day CVE-2023-2868 are ineffective (reporting FBI alert)
Barracuda fixed a new ESG zero-day exploited by Chinese group UNC4841 (reporting Barracuda advisory)

provenance.importedSummary: UNC4841 is a well-resourced threat actor that has utilized a wide range of malware and purpose-built tooling to enable their global espionage operations. They have been observed selectively deploying specific malware families at high priority targets, with SKIPJACK being the most widely deployed. UNC4841 primarily targeted government and technology organizations, but they have also been observed targeting other verticals.
